'''Frank A. Farris''' is an American mathematician. He is a professor of Mathematics and Computer Science at [[Santa Clara University]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.maa.org/news/interview-frank-farris|title=An Interview with Frank Farris {{!}} Mathematical Association of America|website=www.maa.org|access-date=2020-02-06}}</ref> He is also an editor, author, and artist whose work concerns mathematical topics. Farris is known primarily for mathematical exposition, his creation of visual mathematics through computer science, and advocacy for mathematical art as a discipline.<ref>{{Cite journal |title=Mathematical Art as a Discipline |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/202106/rnoti-p980.pdf |journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society |volume=68 |pages=980–986}}</ref>

==Education==
Farris was born in [[Santa Monica, California]]. Shortly after his birth, his family moved to [[Covina, California|Covina]], a suburb of Los Angeles. He showed interest and proficiency in a large variety of subjects such as astronomy. At age 15, he enrolled in the NSF summer science training program, designed to enrich mathematical talent in America.<ref name=":1" />

Farris studied mathematics as an undergraduate at [[Pomona College]] and received his Ph.D. at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]. His dissertation ''Spiralling Chains in CR Manifolds'' was supervised by [[Richard Burt Melrose]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Frank Farris - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=44391 |access-date=2022-04-06 |website=www.mathgenealogy.org}}</ref> His time at MIT led him to pursue pure mathematics with a focus on geometry.<ref name=":1" />

== Career ==
Farris taught at [[Brown University]] for three years, before becoming an assistant professor in [[Santa Clara University]] in 1984. He was tenured and promoted to associate professor in 1988 and was promoted to full professor in 2017.<ref name=":1" /> He was awarded the Award for Distinguished College or University Teaching by the Golden Section of the [[Mathematical Association of America]] (MAA) in 2018.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2019 |title=Teaching Awards |pages=3 |work=Mini Focus |url=http://sections.maa.org/golden/documents/TeacherCall2019.pdf}}</ref>

Farris was the editor of ''[[Mathematics Magazine]]'' from 2001 to 2005, and then again in 2009.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Editors of Mathematics Magazine {{!}} Mathematical Association of America |url=https://www.maa.org/press/periodicals/mathematics-magazine/editors-of-mathematics-magazine |access-date=2022-04-06 |website=www.maa.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Five Years at the Magazine {{!}} Mathematical Association of America |url=https://www.maa.org/five-years-at-the-magazine |access-date=2022-04-06 |website=www.maa.org}}</ref> His article "The Edge of the Universe" for ''[[Math Horizons]]'' received the Trevor Adams Award from the MAA.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Edge of the Universe {{!}} Mathematical Association of America |url=https://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/writing-awards/the-edge-of-the-universe |access-date=2022-04-06 |website=www.maa.org}}</ref>

In 2015, his book ''Creating Symmetry: The Artful Mathematics of Wallpaper Patterns'', which conveys his artistic method, was published by the [[Princeton University Press]].<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite book |url=https://press.princeton.edu/books/hardcover/9780691161730/creating-symmetry |title=Creating Symmetry |date=2015-06-02 |isbn=978-0-691-16173-0 |language=en|last1=Farris |first1=Frank A. |publisher=Princeton University Press }}</ref> It was awarded the [[PROSE Awards|PROSE Award]] in Mathematics from the [[Association of American Publishers]], Honorable Mention, in 2016, and the [[Alpha Sigma Nu]] Book Award in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 Award Winners |url=https://proseawards.com/winners/2016-award-winners/ |access-date=2022-04-06 |website=PROSE Awards |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2018 Alpha Sigma Nu Book Award Winners |url=https://issuu.com/alphasigmanu/docs/final_-_winter_2018_newsletter/s/34585 |access-date=2022-04-06 |website=issuu |language=en}}</ref> It is profiled in numerous periodicals including [[Quanta Magazine|Quanta]] and [[Scientific American]].<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lamb |first=Evelyn |title=Impossible Wallpaper and Mystery Curves: Exploring Symmetry in Mathematics and Art |url=https://blogs.scientificamerican.com/roots-of-unity/creating-symmetry-frank-farris/ |access-date=2022-04-06 |website=Scientific American Blog Network |language=en}}</ref>

== Work method ==
Farris generates organic mathematical art using symmetry, patterns, and wave functions.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oberlinreview.org/6083/news/off-the-cuff-frank-a-farris-professor-of-mathematics-and-computer-science-at-santa-clara-university/|title=Off the Cuff: Frank A. Farris, professor of mathematics and computer science at Santa Clara University|last=Dobbins|first=Elizabeth|website=The Oberlin Review|access-date=2020-02-06}}</ref> He commonly works with wallpaper patterns using photographs as source material.<ref>{{Cite web|title=A p4/p2 of Puzzle Pieces, 2012 {{!}} Viz {{!}} Carleton College|url=https://apps.carleton.edu/campus/viz/exhibitions/white_spaces/seeing_symmetry/p4/|access-date=2021-04-07|website=apps.carleton.edu}}</ref> The wallpaper often exhibit translational symmetry across two independent axes.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://math.scu.edu/~ffarris/CMSReview.pdf |title=Creating Symmetry: The Artful Mathematics of Wallpaper Patterns |access-date=2020-02-05 |archive-date=2020-02-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200205194835/http://math.scu.edu/~ffarris/CMSReview.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> He has created work that gives the illusion of five-fold [[rotational symmetry]] in the [[Wallpaper group]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|last=Klarreich|first=Erica|title=How to Make Impossible Wallpaper|url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/how-to-make-impossible-wallpaper-20130305/|access-date=2021-04-07|website=Quanta Magazine|date=5 March 2013|language=en}}</ref> His award-winning<ref>{{Cite web |title=News from the AMS |url=http://www.ams.org/news?news_id=4011 |access-date=2022-04-06 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en}}</ref> artwork has been profiled by the [[American Mathematical Society]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mathematical Imagery: Frank Farris: Seeing Symmetry |url=http://www.ams.org/publicoutreach/math-imagery/farris |access-date=2022-04-06 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en}}</ref>

He promotes a visual and computational perspective of math through his art, seminars, writing, etc. typically aimed towards undergraduates and mathematicians.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=SCU Personal Homepage for Farris, Frank |url=http://math.scu.edu/~ffarris/ |access-date=2020-02-06 |website=math.scu.edu |archive-date=2019-09-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190930192815/http://math.scu.edu/~ffarris/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== LGBTQIA+ Community ==
Farris is an active member of the [[LGBT community|LGBTQIA+ community]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=MAA Focus February/March 2019 |url=http://digitaleditions.walsworthprintgroup.com/publication/?i=566588&view=archiveBrowser |access-date=2022-04-06 |website=digitaleditions.walsworthprintgroup.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Spectra Out and Ally Lists |url=http://lgbtmath.org/People.html}}</ref> He has worked for the advancement of LGBTQIA+ mathematicians, for instance, in the formation of [[Spectra (mathematical association)]].<ref>{{Cite journal |title=The Origins of Spectra, an Organization for LGBT Mathematicians |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/201906/rnoti-p875.pdf |journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society |volume=66 |pages=875–882}}</ref> In 2014, he married [[William O. Beeman]]; they had been a couple since 1984.<ref name=":3" /> In 2021, he was profiled in the podcast "Count Me In with Della and Deanna".<ref>{{Cite web |title=MAA Blog: Count Me In |url=https://www.mathvalues.org/masterblog/count-me-in-with-della-and-deanna-a-podcast |access-date=2022-04-06 |website=MATH VALUES |date=8 November 2021 |language=en-US}}</ref>
